title: Thoracic Serious Pathology and Visceral Referred Pain
lead: When the thoracic spine is the messenger, not the source.
qa: Pain that wakes the patient but improves on moving in bed is likely? Mechanical. Constant pain unaffected by position is more concerning.
Which cancers commonly spread to bone? Breast, lung, prostate, kidney, thyroid.
Why measure height? Height loss can indicate vertebral compression fractures.
Right shoulder blade pain after fatty meals suggests? Gallbladder disease.
A 25-year-old man with morning stiffness for 2 hours that improves with exercise? Possible axial spondyloarthritis; rheumatology referral.

redFlags.Finding: Thoracic pain with leg weakness or bladder change
Cancer history with new thoracic pain
redFlags.Immediate action: Same-week medical review, sooner if neurological signs

manualNotes: Osteoporotic fracture: pain management, gentle mobility, posture and back extensor strengthening, falls prevention, avoid loaded spinal flexion and twisting early (see Vol 11 Ch 5).
Metastatic disease: maintain function within the oncology team plan; avoid manual therapy over affected levels; know the spinal stability status from the medical team.
Axial spondyloarthritis: regular mobility and strengthening exercise, aerobic exercise, postural training, alongside medical treatment.
